purpose: When a missing rail appears in app planning, route the agent to the right local docs, external sources, first-principles questions, and expected artifact before any product claim is upgraded.

triggers.name: Oracle / price-feed rail
triggers.whyItMatters: Lending, perps, stable-value, insurance, and prediction settlement all fail if price or event data can be stale, manipulated, or unchallengeable.

externalSources.name: Kaskad oracle article
externalSources.useFor: V1 off-chain oracle and liquidation simulation, weighted-median feed, Eliott Mea / KEF research note.

externalSources.name: KasMedia Eliott Mea oracle interview
externalSources.useFor: First-principles oracle risks, CEX price manipulation, median-oracle limits, no-arbitrage ground-truth framing.

externalSources.name: Kaskad docs: roadmap
externalSources.useFor: Oracle V1/V2 timing, L1 expansion conditions, vProg/covenant dependencies.

researchQuestions: What is the data source: CEX book, DEX book, signed reporter set, miner/pool signal, or source-chain proof?
What is the manipulation model and who profits from skewing the feed?
Can stale or wrong data be detected deterministically, or only reviewed socially/economically?
What happens to app state when the feed is stale, split, or challenged?
Is the output used for display, warning, liquidation, settlement, or custody movement?

triggers.name: Kaskad / lending mechanics rail
triggers.whyItMatters: Kaskad is the closest public Kaspa-ecosystem example for lending mechanics, but it runs through Igra/EVM and should be mapped carefully against this TN12 L1 covenant repo.

externalSources.name: Kaskad docs: architecture
externalSources.useFor: Igra EVM L2 execution, lending core, oracle integration, governance layer.

externalSources.name: Kaskad docs: lending mechanics
externalSources.useFor: Supply, borrow, utilization, health factor, permissionless liquidations, risk parameters.

externalSources.name: Kaskad FAQ
externalSources.useFor: User-facing risk, wrapped assets, oracle errors, liquidation explanation, non-custodial claims.

researchQuestions: Which parts are EVM/Igra-specific and which can migrate to Kaspa L1 covenants or vProgs later?
Where does collateral sit in this repo's model versus Kaskad's model?
What exactly triggers liquidation, and who can execute it?
Which risk parameters are hard-coded, bounded-governance, or manually configured?
What does this repo need before a lending dashboard becomes more than simulation?
doNotClaim: Kaskad mechanics directly port to covenants

triggers.name: Miner / RTD signal rail
triggers.whyItMatters: Miner or pool signals may become useful for fast event awareness, but they are not block-header facts or production oracle feeds by default.

externalSources.name: Kaspa Explained llms.txt RTD/oracle nuance
externalSources.useFor: Local source discipline around RTD-derived attestations and oracle research boundaries.

researchQuestions: What are miners or pools actually attesting to: local observation, price, latency, block data, mempool data, or external event?
Is sampling voluntary, rewarded, Sybil-resistant, and signed?
How are conflicting miner/pool reports handled?
Can the signal affect custody or only review prompts?
What anti-bribery, anti-spam, and reputation thresholds are required?

triggers.name: Bridge / source-chain anchor rail
triggers.whyItMatters: ZK proofs and bridge attestations do not automatically establish source-chain canonicality or safe wrapped-asset custody.

externalSources.name: Kaskad docs: roadmap
externalSources.useFor: Hyperlane cross-chain support and L1 migration dependencies.

externalSources.name: Kaskad FAQ
externalSources.useFor: Wrapped-asset user-facing description and bridge/custody assumptions.

researchQuestions: What object is anchored: block header, finality certificate, proof, reporter quorum, or wrapped-asset mint?
Who can challenge or revert a bad source-chain claim?
Where are locked source assets held and how can users exit?
Does the app need bridge custody, or only a receipt mapper?
What happens during source-chain reorgs or bridge outages?

triggers.name: DEX / AMM / liquidity rail
triggers.whyItMatters: DEXs attract liquidity, but require enforceable reserve accounting, ordering rules, LP accounting, and user-safe settlement.
researchQuestions: Are reserves covenant state, indexer state, rollup state, vProg state, or issuer records?
What enforces minimum output and slippage?
How are LP shares minted, burned, and redeemed?
How is ordering handled under fast blockDAG inclusion?
What can be built first as an accepted intent registry without custody?

rules: When a trigger phrase appears in planning, consult the local sources before widening research.
Use external sources as leads, then encode the result in a repo artifact before upgrading claims.
Research can include docs, code, simulations, miner/pool signal design, and direct protocol questions.
No app claim moves from research to build-now without a first artifact and do-not-claim boundary.
